comments.author: @TravelHorizon-4K
comments.text: Framing Moldova as the "cheapest country in Europe" is great for digital nomads and budget travelers, but "cheap" for foreigners often means painfully low wages for locals. Does the influx of remote workers and budget tourists actually help Moldova’s economy, or does it just drive up housing costs and inflation for local residents?

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: That is a very thoughtful perspective on the trade-offs between tourism and the local cost of living, and we appreciate you raising such an important point about the economic impact on the community.

comments.author: @TravelUnknown-1602
comments.text: Moldova interests me because “cheap” only tells part of the story. I’m more curious about what everyday life actually feels like there—the food, villages, cities, family life, and pace of living. Would you visit Moldova for the low prices, or for the culture itself?

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Without question, it is the culture and human warmth that make the journey worthwhile, @TravelUnknown-1602. The deep winemaking heritage, the slow and grounded rhythm of the villages, and the genuine hospitality of the people offer far more richness than any budget travel label ever could. Thank you for asking such a thoughtful question!

comments.author: @scioparto
comments.text: It was cheap very long time ago. Now it’s one of the most expensive countries in Europe especially if you live on the local income. The gas, the oil, imported fruits and vegetables are much more expensive than in EU. It’s a small not rich market, so everything has more higher price than in a big market. Moldova doesn’t have even H&M, Ikea , Zara, Amazon, nothing, just local resellers with a much higher prices and much smaller selection.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Thank you for bringing this grounded economic reality to light, @scioparto. You raise a crucial point—what may look cheap to visitors with foreign earnings can be exceedingly harsh on local salaries, especially regarding imported necessities and utility bills. We really appreciate you providing that authentic perspective!
